tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill whenever...'), focuses on triggering contexts (error messages, call types, scenarios) rather than internal implementation, is pushy by explicitly listing many trigger cases including negative scope ('Not for 503 SlowDown, replication...'), and remains a concise paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill whenever an S3 request fails with AccessDenied or 403 Forbidden: GetObject, PutObject, ListBucket, HeadObject or CopyObject calls... Not for 503 SlowDown, replication or lifecycle issues, CloudFront 403s, Lake Formation access, Bedrock or SageMaker role denials, or a least-privilege review with no observed failure.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps straight into domain-specific procedures (ten layers, verdicts, gotchas) without explaining general concepts like what S3 or IAM is. It is concise and dense with non-obvious, skill-specific content.
tests.evidence: The ten layers... S3 evaluates every layer that applies to the request. Any explicit deny wins, and the request also needs an allow.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference material (the per-layer API calls, denial message hints, fallback sources) is deferred to references/ files and only summarized in the body. No large reference blocks or embedded lookup tables exist in the body itself.
tests.evidence: Load [references/layers.md](references/layers.md#the-ten-layers) at Step 4 for the API call that reads each layer and its typical denial.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Both reference files (denial-message-hints.md and layers.md) have explicit markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link specifies the condition/timing for loading it, e.g., only when a message exists, at Step 4, at Step 6, or only when all layers are clean.
tests.evidence: load it only when a message or CloudTrail `errorMessage` exists... Load [references/layers.md](references/layers.md#other-causes-outside-the-ten-layers) only when every layer comes back clean.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths from the skill root with anchor fragments, no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (read-only policy, verdict assignment, validation) are prescriptive with exact rules, while flexible parts like evidence collection order and fix proposal explain rationale rather than rigid steps.
tests.evidence: Read-only. Never call `PutBucketPolicy`, `PutPublicAccessBlock`, `PutKeyPolicy`, `PutRolePolicy`, or any other write API.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill prescribes a clear default (read policy documents directly) with SimulatePrincipalPolicy as secondary corroboration, not presented as equal alternatives.
tests.evidence: Collect evidence, policy reads first: read each layer's document directly. Use `SimulatePrincipalPolicy` only as corroboration.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic procedure (classify, pin request, walk layers, assign verdicts, propose fix) applicable to any S3 403 case, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Step 5 - Walk the layers: evaluate all ten layers; do not stop at the first one that passes.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a detailed Gotchas section with concrete, specific corrections relevant to the S3 authorization domain.
tests.evidence: A "blocked by policy" refusal on an S3 read is a platform limit, not a finding about the bucket... `SimulatePrincipalPolicy` ignores VPC endpoint policies and session policies...

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces a structured report and provides an explicit output template/format section in the body itself.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The inline report format template is short (5 bullet items, well under 20 lines) and appropriate to keep inline.
